names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 11 Δεκεμβρίου, «Άγιοι Αειθαλάς και Ακεψεής», with the rank word left off.

Read from the calendar’s own name page, «Аифал Арбесский (Персидский), мч.», with the rank stripped and both epithets kept as the page prints them, the parenthesis included; the day line declines it as «Аифала». `fk.mjs` on the stored string returns NONE.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 11 декабря ст. ст. — «Мчч. Акепсия и Аифала (354).»

attestations.note: The second of the two the day’s second line names, on the same menologion day the Greek calendar keeps the pair on. The reading at /Life/life3103.htm is the first account the folder has had of him and it gives him a grade: «диакон Арбельской церкви», a deacon of the church of Arbela, which is written into `types` as `deacon`. THE OFFICE IS NOT WRITTEN: `Deacon` would have to be in all four locale packs for `tests/i18n.test.mjs`, and the grade is in `types` and in the life instead. `dates` are written for the first time from the line’s «(354)» alone. The day page prints four hymns and none is under either name.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (2 October 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 11ης Δεκεμβρίου — «Άγιοι Αειθαλάς και Ακεψεής»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 11 Δεκεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The entry names both its members and gives each his rank, so it is one folder per named member and each relates the other. The page does not name the Persian king, so no `dates` object. The corpus keeps an `akepsimas-29-january` and, drafted in this run, an Akepsimas of 7 December and an Akepsimas of this same 11 December in the separate entry of Peter the ascetic; this man's companion Ἀκεψεής is a different name again and the four are kept apart. Arbela in Persia is named; no coordinate is proposed. No hymn is printed. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue as printed by pravoslavno.rs (2 October 2026).

death.note: The year the Russian day line closes with, «Мчч. Акепсия и Аифала (354)»; the folder had no date at all before, the Greek calendar giving none, and the reading behind the line gives none either.
